hints.title: Find the roots symbolically
hints.body: Apply the quadratic formula to x2−2px+q=0. Keep p as any real number; its sign is not restricted.
hints.pitfall: Do not assume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math> merely because a square root appears.

recall.reminder: The quadratic formula gives both roots, including their common centre.

hints.title: Express their separation
hints.body: The roots are p±p2−q, so their positive difference is 2p2−q.
hints.recap: The common <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>p</mi></mrow></math> cancels in the root difference.
hints.pitfall: The difference is twice the square-root term.
hints.pause: Translate greater than 2 and less than 4 into one chain.

recall.reminder: Compute the requested root expression rather than unrelated individual quantities.

hints.title: Preserve strict endpoints
hints.body: Divide the separation inequality by two before squaring its positive bounds; then isolate p2 or q.
hints.recap: Equivalent steps must keep strict endpoints.
hints.pitfall: Equality would allow an excluded separation.
hints.pause: Rearrange fully and verify both directions of the condition.

recall.reminder: Equivalent steps must keep strict endpoints.

solution:
The roots are p−p2−q and p+p2−q. Their positive separation is 2p2−q.

Thus the target is equivalent to 2<2p2−q<4, then to 1<p2−q<4. This already ensures that the roots are real and distinct.

Rearranging gives q<p2−1<q+3. Every step is reversible, so D is both necessary and sufficient.
knowledgePattern: Convert strict root separation to a biconditional discriminant bound
